items.stem: In gradient descent, why do we move in the direction opposite to the gradient?

options.text: The negative gradient points toward lower loss
options.rationale: Correct: descent follows the downhill direction.

options.text: The gradient points toward the global maximum of accuracy
options.rationale: The gradient points uphill in loss, not toward accuracy.

options.text: Direction does not affect the result
options.rationale: Direction determines whether loss rises or falls.

options.text: It increases the loss on purpose
options.rationale: Descent reduces loss, not increases it.

items.explanation: Correct: descent follows the downhill direction.

items.stem: Which TWO problems can a poorly chosen learning rate cause? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Divergence or overshooting the minimum if too large
options.rationale: Correct: too large a step can overshoot.

options.text: Extremely slow training if too small
options.rationale: Correct: tiny steps converge very slowly.
No learning rate guarantees instant convergence.
Learning rate does not remove local minima.
